deals.headline: Milan Mandaric sells Sheffield Wednesday to Dejphon Chansiri
deals.summary: Thai businessman Dejphon Chansiri bought the club from Milan Mandaric, owner since November 2010. The price is not stated on the cited page.

deals.evidence: Chansiri agreed to pay £60m for Hillsborough, with the club's 2017-18 accounts showing that an initial payment of £7.5m was due within one year.
deals.headline: Club sells Hillsborough to owner Chansiri for about £60m
deals.summary: To stay within the EFL's spending rules the club sold Hillsborough to a company controlled by its owner, Sheffield 3 Limited, booking a profit of more than £38m in its 2017-18 accounts and leasing the ground back; the sale later led to a 12-point deduction.

deals.evidence: A pending charge against the stadium - a legal way of securing a loan - was lodged with the Land Registry on 30 September.
deals.headline: Chansiri secures debt against Hillsborough
deals.investor: Undisclosed lender via New Avenue Projects Limited
deals.summary: A pending charge against Hillsborough, owned by Chansiri's Sheffield 3 Limited, was lodged with the Land Registry by New Avenue Projects Limited, an intermediary that matches clubs with lenders; the lender and amount were not disclosed.

deals.evidence: Sheffield Wednesday have announced that US consortium Arise Capital Partners has bought the club, officially bringing to an end Dejphon Chansiri's ownership.
deals.headline: Arise Capital Partners buys Sheffield Wednesday out of administration
deals.investor: Arise Capital Partners (David Storch, Michael Storch, Tom Costin)
deals.seller: Joint administrators of Sheffield Wednesday Football Club Limited (BTG Begbies Traynor); former owner Dejphon Chansiri
deals.summary: After six months in administration (from 24 October 2025) and the collapse of a £47.8m bid led by James Bord, the administrators sold the club to the Storch-led Arise consortium. The EFL waived the 15-point exit penalty; the club stays under budget restrictions for two seasons. The administrators' progress report says the consideration will be set out in their next report.

founded_evidence: Sheffield Wednesday Football Club was formed in 1867 as an offshoot of the Wednesday Cricket Club.
name: Sheffield Wednesday Football Club
notes: League corrected: Wednesday were relegated from the Championship in February 2026 and play the 2026-27 season in EFL League One (BBC, 2 May 2026). Latest accounts are for the year to 31 July 2024 (2023-24); the 2024-25 accounts were never filed because the operating company (02509978) went into administration on 24 October 2025 and remains in administration. The business was sold to a new Arise group: Companies House shows SWFC Sports Holdings 2026 Limited (PSC David Storch, 75% or more via a trust) owning Wednesday 1867 Limited (17111133) and Hillsborough 1899 Limited (17110405), all registered at Hillsborough Stadium; which company now holds the club's EFL share and the stadium is not stated on any page I could read. Stadium owner left null: Hillsborough was owned by Chansiri's Sheffield 3 Limited (BBC, 2020), which is itself in administration, and no page states who owns it after the sale. Sale price not disclosed (administrators' June 2026 progress report, scanned PDF, defers it to the next report; an exclusivity fee of £4.14m was paid into the administration). Capacity: BBC (July 2025) gives 34,835; the Premier League's older stadium page gives 39,732. Tom Costin is co-founder of Owl Ventures and an investor in Blue Crow Sports Group (BBC), but no page states that Blue Crow itself holds a stake in Wednesday. Stakes within the consortium are not stated. Shirt sponsor, kit supplier, social counts not found; swfc.co.uk renders client-side.

ownership_summary: Bought out of administration on 1 May 2026 by a three-man US consortium under Arise Capital Partners: David Storch (chairman), his son Michael Storch and Tom Costin, ending Dejphon Chansiri's ownership (2015-2026). Companies House lists David Storch, through control over the trustees of a trust, with 75% or more of SWFC Sports Holdings 2026 Limited, the new holding company registered at Hillsborough. The former operating company, Sheffield Wednesday Football Club Limited, remains in administration.
